chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Hashim, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever removes a speck from the face of his believing brother, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will write for him ten good deeds; and whoever smiles in the face of his brother, it will be a good deed for him.

key_terms.أَخِيهِ الْمُؤْمِنِ: His believing brother, referring to a fellow Muslim in the context of spiritual kinship
key_terms.تَبَسَّمَ: He smiled, indicating a gentle, non-verbal expression of goodwill
key_terms.عَشْرَ حَسَنَاتٍ: Ten good deeds, a specific measure of reward
key_terms.قَذَاةً: A speck or small particle, often referring to dust or impurity on the face

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for removing a speck from a believer's face or smiling at them?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith to illustrate the profound spiritual weight of mundane acts of care, where removing a speck of dust (qadha) from a believer's face is equated to ten good deeds. This tradition underscores the Shia emphasis on physical and emotional gentleness as a means of honoring the divine image in others, while the smile is elevated as a distinct, rewardable act of social lubrication that strengthens communal bonds.
